newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The Bank of Greece's decisive support of the drachma against wholesale selling by London-based US banks was a statement of intention to money markets yesterday that the country's central bank was not about to slacken its exchange policies.

--The national economy and development ministries are at loggerheads over the spat between industry and retailers in the food sector regarding industry's charges of unfair competition. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said competition was not operating as it should while Deputy Development Minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis defended the operation of the market.

--1998 will be a difficult year in the lead up to economic and monetary union, Papandoniou said yesterday after meeting on budget targets with senior government and financial sector officials. According to sources, both government and the administration of the central bank believe that this year's fiscal targets can be achieved.
--Forex outflows yesterday, combined with already restricted liquidity in the interbank market, pushed interest rates up by almost two points.

--The government has decided on a "national responsibility" initiative to reduce inflation at yesterday's meeting on the budget at the national economy ministry. Sources say the government will call all those bodies and organisations able to influence inflation to the table to keep a lid on prices.
--Deputy Development Minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis will have meetings with retailers and industrialists in the foodstuffs sector today to mediate in the frosty relations between the two.

--The priorities in the government's economic policies were the focus on yesterday's meeting on the budgets yesterday, according to reports. The reports said the government placed emphasis on reducing inflation below 3.0 percent and to the deficit below 3.0 percent of GDP.

--There will be significant changes in the present operation of common agricultural policy and cohesion funds, the European Commission announced yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
